title: About
text:
I’m an AI Engineer. Right now I work with data that comes from rockets.
At Avio S.p.A. I build machine learning models for space launcher engineering: surrogate models that learn from numerical simulations and experimental data, computer vision systems that monitor industrial tests, and RAG and agentic AI systems that let engineers query internal technical documentation in plain language.
I got here through mathematics — a BSc in Siena, an MSc in Applied Mathematics in Bologna, and then eight years across very different domains: banking, telco, oil & gas, automotive, tires, and now aerospace. The hard part was always understanding the problem and data well enough to know what question to ask the data in the first place. That is Data Science for me.

title: About
text:
How I work
I care more about validation than accuracy. A model scoring 0.95 on a random split and collapsing on an unseen operating condition is worth nothing — and in aerospace, slightly less than nothing. The part of the job I spend the most time on is designing validation strategies that reflect how the model will actually be used.
I care about interpretability. I work with engineers who understand the physics of their systems far better than any model does. An output they can’t interrogate is an output they won’t adopt, and they’re right not to.
I care about things shipping. A notebook that only runs on my laptop isn’t a project. It’s an experiment.
